verdict.summary: Composio has no managed Pipedrive app, so you have to register your own in Developer Hub, which needs a free developer sandbox account. A private app set to Live can be installed by any company through an unlisted link without review. Only a public Marketplace listing goes through review, which takes up to 21 business days. Choose public or private carefully, because you cannot change the app type later.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a private app; 1-3 days to prepare a public Marketplace submission (listing assets, policies, demo video, install/uninstall flows)
verdict.approval_wait: None for draft or private (unlisted) apps; up to 21 business days for a public Marketplace review

gates.name: Draft app (sandbox company)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize the app and call the API with users of the company where the app was created (your developer sandbox).
limits: A draft app can only be seen and installed by users in the company that created it (community answer, not official docs)
Access tokens last 60 minutes; refresh tokens expire after 60 days without use
Only one callback URL per app
You need a developer sandbox account before Developer Hub appears

gates.name: Private app set to Live (unlisted install link)
gates.unlocks: Any Pipedrive company can install the app through a direct, unlisted installation link. It does not appear in the Marketplace.
limits: Not listed or searchable in the Marketplace
App type (private vs public) is fixed when you create the app
A third-party guide says Pipedrive's partner agreement requires approval for apps sold to customers, even unlisted ones. This is unverified against the agreement itself.
Per-company API token budget and burst rate limits still apply

gates.name: Public Marketplace app (approved and published)
gates.unlocks: The app is listed in the Pipedrive Marketplace, where anyone can find and install it.
limits: Needs a demo video explaining scope usage, working test accounts, and a reachable contact during review
Needs Terms of Service and Privacy Policy pages, an icon of at least 256x256 px, and 16:10 screenshots
Installation and uninstallation flows are mandatory
After approval the app stays unlisted until you click Publish
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 21 business days of review after submission, plus your preparation time

steps.title: Get a Pipedrive developer sandbox account
steps.detail: Sign up for a free developer sandbox at developers.pipedrive.com. Developer Hub only appears in a sandbox account.
gotchas: Developer Hub does not appear in a normal Pipedrive account. Use the sandbox.

steps.title: Decide on private or public, then create the app
steps.detail: In the sandbox, open Settings > Developer Hub and click "Create an app" (or "+ Create an app"). Choose a private app if an unlisted install link is enough. Choose "Create public app" only if you need a Marketplace listing.
gotchas: You cannot change the app type later in Developer Hub.
Private apps skip review. Public apps must pass review before they can be listed.

steps.title: Fill in Basic info and set the callback URL
steps.detail: In the Basic info tab, enter the app name and paste Composio's callback URL as the OAuth callback URL, then save.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Pipedrive allows only one callback URL per app.
A placeholder URL is fine for a draft, but it must be a working URL before you submit for approval.

steps.title: Choose a minimal scope set
steps.detail: Compare the Composio Pipedrive actions you plan to use with Pipedrive's scope reference, and select only the scopes those actions need. Composio's defaults are contacts:full, leads:full, mail:full, activities:full, products:full and projects:full. The base scope is always on.
gotchas: Users must accept or deny all scopes at once, so extra scopes can cause users to refuse the whole request.
Avoid the admin scope unless you need it, because it only works when the installing user is a company admin.

steps.title: Save scopes and copy client_id and client_secret
steps.detail: In the OAuth & access scopes tab, tick the chosen scopes and save. Copy the client_id and client_secret shown there.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your own credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for Pipedrive (OAuth2) and check "Use your own developer authentication". Paste in the client_id and client_secret, and trim the scope list to match what you selected in Pipedrive.
gotchas: Composio has no managed Pipedrive app, so you must use your own credentials.
The scopes in Composio should match the ones enabled in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio, log in with a sandbox company user, approve the scopes, then make a test API call. Composio exchanges the code with HTTP Basic auth at oauth.pipedrive.com.
gotchas: A 401 'unauthorized access' from the authorize endpoint usually means a wrong client_id.
A draft app may only be installable by users of the company that created it.

steps.title: Set the private app to Live and share the install link
steps.detail: In Developer Hub, move the private app to Live status. Share its unlisted installation link with the companies that need it. No review is required.
gotchas: If you sell the app to customers, check the Developer Partner Agreement. A third-party guide says sold apps need approval even when unlisted.
Per-company rate limits apply. When the daily budget is used up, requests return 429 until midnight server time.

steps.title: Draft the Privacy Policy, Terms of Service and listing text
steps.detail: For a public app, draft the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service pages and the listing copy. Prepare a 1:1 icon of at least 256x256 px and 3-5 screenshots at a 16:10 aspect ratio.
gotchas: The registration form accepts 1-5 images, but the review checklist asks for 3-5.

steps.title: Meet the technical review checklist
steps.detail: Check that the app refreshes access tokens when their 60-minute lifetime ends, never collects users' personal API tokens, has working installation and uninstallation flows, and authorizes without interruption. Set a working callback URL.
gotchas: The checklist requires that no other public or private apps get installed for the user alongside the listed app.

steps.title: Record the demo video and prepare test accounts
steps.detail: Record a demo video that explains how the app uses each permission and scope. Set up working test accounts for reviewers and name a contact who can be reached during the review.

steps.title: Preview the listing and click Send to review
steps.detail: Preview the Marketplace listing in Developer Hub, then click "Send to review".

steps.title: Wait for Pipedrive's review
steps.detail: Reviews can take up to 21 business days. If the app is rejected, you get an email with the reasons, and you must fix them before you resubmit.

steps.title: Publish the approved app
steps.detail: After approval the app stays unlisted. Click Publish in Developer Hub to make it visible in the Marketplace.

requirements.detail: Free. Developer Hub is only visible in a sandbox account.
Enter it in the Basic info tab. Only one is allowed per app, so use Composio's callback URL.
A community answer says public and unlisted apps need OAuth 2.0 to be approved.

requirements.item: Privacy Policy and Terms of Service pages

requirements.detail: A 1:1 icon of at least 256x256 px and 3-5 screenshots at 16:10.

requirements.item: Demo video, test accounts, review contact
requirements.detail: The video must explain how the app uses its permissions and scopes.
Install and uninstall flows are mandatory. The app must refresh 60-minute access tokens and must not store users' personal API tokens.

scopes.effect: Always on. Gives read access to the user's profile, account currencies and settings.
A Composio default. Pipedrive does not label scopes as sensitive. For a public app, explain its use in the demo video.
A Composio default. Keep it only if you use lead actions, and justify it in the demo video for review.
A Composio default that grants mailbox access. Drop it unless you need it, because users must accept all scopes at once.
A Composio default. Keep it only if you use activity actions.
A Composio default. Keep it only if you use product actions.
A Composio default. Keep it only if you use project actions.
Can only be granted when the installing user is a company admin. Non-admin installs will fail, so your app must handle that.

blockers.symptom: You need a Marketplace listing but created a private app (or the reverse).
blockers.cause: The app type is fixed when you create the app.
blockers.fix: Create a new app with the correct type and update the client_id and client_secret in Composio.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect or callback mismatch, or the authorize endpoint returns 401 'unauthorized access'.
blockers.cause: The callback URL differs from Composio's, or the client_id is wrong. Pipedrive allows only one callback URL.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from the Composio auth config into Basic info, and re-check the client_id and client_secret.

blockers.symptom: Users from other companies cannot install the app.
blockers.cause: The app is still a draft, and draft apps install only within the creating company (per a community answer).
blockers.fix: Set the private app to Live and share its install link, or get a public app approved.

blockers.symptom: A connection stops working after a period of inactivity.
blockers.cause: The refresh token expired after 60 days without use.
blockers.fix: Have the user reconnect (reinstall the app). Use connections regularly so the refresh token stays alive.

blockers.cause: The company's daily API token budget or burst limit is used up. OAuth apps share it with API-token use.
blockers.fix: Throttle and batch requests. The daily budget resets at midnight server time.

blockers.symptom: A rejection email from Pipedrive review.
blockers.cause: One or more checklist items are missing, such as the demo video, policies, install flows or token refresh.
blockers.fix: Fix each listed reason, then click Send to review again.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Pipedrive, so you need your own app from the start. Register it in Developer Hub, then create a Composio OAuth2 auth config with 'Use your own developer authentication' checked and paste in the client_id and client_secret. Copy the exact callback URL from the Composio dashboard into Pipedrive's single callback URL field. Trim Composio's six *:full default scopes to the ones you actually use.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit record shows Pipedrive has no managed auth scheme; the only OAuth2 entry requires the developer's own credentials, with authorization and token endpoints on oauth.pipedrive.com.
evidence.quote: "managed_oauth_available":false

evidence.claim: A Pipedrive developer-community answer says both public and unlisted apps must use OAuth 2.0, and that OAuth is required for approval.
evidence.quote: For both public and unlisted apps, you will need to use OAuth 2.0 authentication. It is required to get your app approved.

evidence.claim: Before a public app is submitted, the developer must build and test it, preview the listing, and then press Send to review.
evidence.quote: Click on “Send to review”

evidence.claim: Pipedrive says public app reviews can take up to 21 business days, citing demand and staff holidays.
evidence.quote: public app reviews may take up to 21 business days.

evidence.claim: Reviewers require a demo video that explains how the app uses permissions and scopes, plus working test accounts and a reachable contact for the review period.
evidence.quote: Provide our team with a demo video in which you explain the usage of permissions and scopes

evidence.claim: The checklist requires a Terms of Service page and a Privacy Policy page for the app.
evidence.quote: Your app has a Privacy Policy webpage of a legal document

evidence.claim: The app icon must be a 1:1 image of at least 256x256 px, and listing screenshots must follow a 16:10 aspect ratio; the registration form allows one to five images while the checklist asks for three to five.
evidence.quote: min 256x256 px

evidence.claim: Reviewers check that the app refreshes the access token when its 60-minute lifetime ends, and that the app does not collect or store a user's personal API token.
evidence.quote: Your app refreshes the access token once its 60-minute lifetime expires

evidence.claim: Installation and uninstallation flows are a mandatory prerequisite for public Marketplace listing.
evidence.quote: it is **mandatory** to have proper installation flows as a **prerequisite** for being listed on the Marketplace as a public app.

evidence.claim: Approval does not make a public app visible; the developer must press Publish in Developer Hub afterward.
evidence.quote: The app is unlisted from the Marketplace by default after approval.

evidence.claim: A rejected app gets an email with the reasons, and the reasons must be resolved before resubmission.
evidence.quote: Before the app can be submitted again, you’ll need to resolve the reason(s) for the rejection

evidence.claim: Composio's setup guide has the developer create the Pipedrive OAuth app first, then select Pipedrive in Composio's Create Auth Config flow with the own-credentials option enabled and the Client ID and Secret pasted in.
evidence.quote: check **Use your own developer authentication**, since that’s the main purpose here.

evidence.claim: The base scope is switched on for every app and gives read access to the authorized user's profile, account currencies, and settings.
evidence.quote: This is the default permission that is always enabled for all apps.

evidence.claim: A user cannot approve some scopes and refuse others; the consent screen accepts or denies the whole scope set.
evidence.quote: The user has the option to **either accept or deny all scopes**.

evidence.claim: The admin scope can only be granted when the installing user is a company admin, so the app must handle non-admin installers who hit failures on it.
evidence.quote: The admin scope requires the user who is installing an app (from the Pipedrive's Marketplace), to have admin rights within the company.

evidence.claim: The scope reference lists broad data-access scopes such as recents:read (recent account activity) and users:read, and it does not flag any scope as restricted or sensitive.
evidence.quote: recents:read **See recent account activity**

evidence.claim: Draft, unlisted, and public apps can change their scopes at any time, and existing users get an email asking them to reauthorize.
evidence.quote: Apps (draft/private, unlisted and public) can update their scopes at any time.

evidence.claim: The OAuth callback URL is entered in the Basic info tab, and Pipedrive accepts only one callback URL per app.
evidence.quote: we allow only one callback URL per app.

evidence.claim: A placeholder callback URL can be used when saving a draft, but a working URL must be substituted before the app goes for approval.
evidence.quote: make sure you change it to a functioning one before submitting it for approval.

evidence.claim: After saving the Basic info tab, the form moves to OAuth & access scopes, where the client_id and client_secret are shown.
evidence.quote: you’ll get your `client_id` and `client_secret`.

evidence.claim: Authorization codes expire five minutes after issue and must be exchanged at the token endpoint using HTTP Basic auth with client_id and client_secret.
evidence.quote: Note that the `authorization_code` expires in **5 minutes**.

evidence.claim: A refresh token lapses if unused for 60 days, and each use resets that window; after lapse the user must reinstall the app from the beginning.
evidence.quote: `refresh_token` will expire if it isn't used in **60 days**.

evidence.claim: A developer sandbox account is required before Developer Hub appears, and the sandbox can be requested for free at developers.pipedrive.com.
evidence.quote: You must have a developer sandbox account for app creation to see Developer Hub.

evidence.claim: Probing the authorize endpoint with an invalid client_id returned HTTP 401 with a JSON error, so the endpoint is live and rejects unknown clients.
evidence.quote: {"success":false,"error":"unauthorized access","errorCode":401

evidence.claim: The developers.pipedrive.com landing page answers HTTP 200 without a login wall and offers a sandbox signup.
evidence.quote: Sign up for a Sandbox Account today to begin experimenting and developing in a risk free environment

evidence.claim: OAuth apps are subject to the same per-company daily token budget as API tokens (30,000 base tokens × plan multiplier × seats), and burst limits of 80 to 480 requests per 2 seconds depending on plan.
evidence.quote: | Lite     | 20 requests per 2 seconds  | 80 requests per 2 seconds  |

evidence.claim: Once the daily budget is used up, requests return HTTP 429 until the midnight server-time reset, and the docs say the Cloudflare 403 block applies to high-volume api_token integrations.
evidence.quote: Only the high volume traffic coming from `api_token` integrations will be blocked.

evidence.claim: No official numeric install or user cap for unreviewed draft, private, or unlisted OAuth apps was found; a community answer says a draft app can only be installed by users of the company that created it.
evidence.quote: An app in draft status can only be seen and installed by users in the same company where it was created.

evidence.claim: The public app registration form has seven tabs spread across two groups.
evidence.quote: The app registration form for public apps is divided into two categories containing seven different tabs.

evidence.claim: The checklist requires that no other public or private app is installed for the user alongside the listed app, and that authorization runs without interruption.
evidence.quote: No other public or private apps will be installed for the user, except the one listed

evidence.claim: To create an app, the developer opens Developer Hub under Settings in the sandbox account and clicks Create an app, then chooses Create public app or the private equivalent.
evidence.quote: click on the green “Create an app” button (or “+ Create an app” if you have existing apps) followed by “Create public app”.

evidence.claim: Pipedrive advises starting with the smallest scope set the app needs and adding scopes only as the endpoints it calls require them.
evidence.quote: Start by choosing the least amount of scopes needed, then enable additional scopes

evidence.claim: The app type is set at creation and cannot be switched between public and private later in Developer Hub.
evidence.quote: Do pick your app type carefully, as it cannot be changed later on Developer Hub.

evidence.claim: Private apps can be shared with any company through a direct, unlisted installation link and do not have to go through the approval process.
evidence.quote: Private apps can be shared with any user/company in Pipedrive via a direct, unlisted installation link. They don’t have to go through the app approval process

evidence.claim: Pipedrive's approval page says that an app used only internally does not need to be submitted, and that a private app can be used instead.
evidence.quote: Submitting the app is unnecessary if it’s only used internally.

evidence.claim: A private app can be moved to Live status so other companies can install it, but it is still not listed in the Marketplace and skips the review.
evidence.quote: A private app can be transitioned to “Live” status, which allows other companies to install it as well

evidence.claim: A third-party guide reads Pipedrive's agreement as requiring approval for an app sold to customers, even if it is never publicly listed.
evidence.quote: An app you sell to customers needs approval even if you never list it publicly.

open_questions: Which exact redirect URI to register: Composio's toolkit record lists backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add, but /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback was also seen. Check the value in your Composio dashboard.
Can a draft app created in the sandbox be authorized against your real (non-sandbox) Pipedrive company, or must it be a Live private app first? This is unconfirmed.
No official numeric install or user cap was found for draft, private or unlisted apps.
PKCE support is not documented. The documented token exchange uses client_secret via HTTP Basic auth.
The Pipedrive Developer Partner Agreement was not reviewed. The claim that sold apps need approval even when unlisted comes only from a third-party guide.
Review outcome statistics and rejection reasons beyond the checklist were not found.
Pipedrive does not label any scope as sensitive or restricted, so it is unconfirmed whether some scopes trigger extra review.
Whether unlisted apps must allow installation by logged-out users has no official answer.
